notes: LUM-1327 — pointer placement in the composer, driven through a real PTY into the real binary (100x20).

Geometry: the composer is docked above the status bar and now carries its border (LUM-1328 follow-up): a one-row draft sits on row 17 (0-based) with the rules on rows 16 and 18, a two-row draft on rows 16-17 with the rules on 15 and 18; the status bar is row 19. The label '> ' owns columns 0-1, so body column N sits at cell x = 2 + N.
Every panel asserts on the character grid: the caret is the '▍' glyph the renderer inserts at the cursor offset, so 'where is the caret' is a text assertion rather than a screenshot opinion.
The matching baseline run of the pre-fix binary is lum1327-composer-click-baseline.json — the same gestures with 'the click changed nothing' as the expectation.
Ctrl+C clears the draft (upstream handleCtrlC: the text is dropped, the process stays alive) and Ctrl+J inserts the line break, so both are used to shape the draft between panels.
caption: LUM-1327 — composer pointer placement (codex chat_composer/mouse.rs + upstream Editor.handleMouse parity), real binary + real PTY + pyte. Panel 1: a click in the middle of 'hello world' puts the caret on the clicked character (it was at the end before). Panel 2: a click on the label gutter puts it on column 0. Panel 3: the same on the second row of a two-line draft — the click accounts for the visual row it landed on. Panel 4: Ctrl+C clears the draft. Panel 5: a 120-column draft wraps over two rows and a click on the first row's last cell leaves the caret on that row instead of spilling onto the next one. Panel 6: a click on the status bar, outside the composer, changes nothing. Nothing mocked.

panels.label: 1. type a draft, then click in the middle of 'hello world'

expect.why: the caret left the end of the draft

panels.label: 2. click on the label gutter: the caret goes to column 0
3. Ctrl+E to the line end, Ctrl+J for a second line, then click on 'cond' of that row

expect.why: the caret moved onto the clicked character of the second row

panels.label: 4. Ctrl+C clears the draft (the process stays alive)
5. a click on the last cell of a wrapped row keeps the caret on that row

expect.why: the caret is on the first visual row's last character, not on the next visual row
and it did not spill onto the row below

panels.label: 6. a click on the status bar (outside the composer) moves nothing

expect.why: exactly one caret, still on the row the previous click placed it on
a click below the composer never places a caret in the status bar
